item.title: Lafcadio Hearn Museum & Residence: Old Japan Through Foreign Eyes — Guide
item.description: Lafcadio Hearn, known in Japan as Koizumi Yakumo, was a writer of Greek-Irish background who came to Matsue in 1890, married into a samurai family, took Japanese citizenship, and did more than almost anyone to introduce the culture and folk tales of old Japan to Western readers. His collections of Japanese ghost stories, especially Kwaidan, remain widely read. Beside the castle moat stand two linked sites: the small samurai residence he rented, preserved with the garden he lovingly described, and a modern memorial museum next door displaying his manuscripts, belongings and the story of his life between two worlds.
